rationale: C22 plausibly supplied a material structural template for the child: both are personal letters assigning an administrator to a Senate-confirmed mobilization post, justify the choice by reference to the appointee's existing experience and responsibilities, and emphasize consolidating related procurement or production functions under unified leadership. C16 also assigns an additional leadership role to an incumbent official, while C11 shares the child's rationale of concentrating and coordinating production functions, but neither matches the overall appointment-letter structure as closely as C22.

shared_material.child_excerpt: your willingness to assume the post of Administrator of the Defense Production Administration... This appointment is subject, of course, to confirmation by the Senate
shared_material.parent_excerpt: I am writing at this time to ask you to accept the position of Administrator in order that I may promptly submit your name to the Senate.
shared_material.explanation: Both letters ask a named official to assume an administrator position and expressly connect the appointment to Senate confirmation.

shared_material.child_excerpt: that you occupy the Defense Production Administration post simultaneously with the position you now occupy as Administrator of the National Production Authority
shared_material.parent_excerpt: Because of the current importance of mobilization activities affecting the procurement and production of critical and strategic materials, special attention must be given this field.
shared_material.explanation: Both frame the appointment around existing mobilization, procurement, and production responsibilities.

shared_material.child_excerpt: a single production head now promises to be the most effective means of overall coordination of mobilization production
shared_material.parent_excerpt: It is my desire that insofar as possible rubber purchases and operations also be consolidated under the RFC.
shared_material.explanation: Both use consolidation under one administrator or agency as the operative administrative solution.
